name: Domijong
description: Domijong is a western domino variant that uses four double-six sets to produce a large duplicated-tile supply. This entry models the core as a connecting domino game; the enlarged supply shifts strategy toward mobility and robust end control rather than precise unique-tile inference.

overview.description: Domijong is a western domino variant that uses four double-six sets to produce a large duplicated-tile supply. This entry models the core as a connecting domino game; the enlarged supply shifts strategy toward mobility and robust end control rather than precise unique-tile inference.

history.origins: Domijong is encountered as a modern large-supply domino format that combines multiple standard sets to support larger groups and longer sessions.
timeline: Modern era: circulated through social play and rules collections.
history.cultural: Played socially in larger groups where the expanded supply keeps the layout active and reduces early stalls.
history.evolution: Using four sets greatly increases duplication, reducing inference and increasing the importance of flexible connectors and long-horizon mobility.

setup.deck: Four double-6 domino sets combined and mixed.
setup.dealing: Deal tiles by player count; remaining tiles may form a boneyard by table profile.
setup.equipment: Domino sets and optional score tracking by table profile.

rules.objective: Play legal matching tiles and end hands under the table profile with the best resulting score.
rules.gameplay: Players place a legal tile to a matching open end of the shared layout. When blocked, the table profile determines whether to draw or pass. Hands end when a player empties their hand or when play becomes blocked, and the match profile determines scoring.
keyRules: Tile placement must match an exposed open end value.
Blocked turns resolve by a draw-or-pass profile.
Hand-end and scoring depend on the match profile in use.

strategy.basic: Preserve mobility and avoid accumulating high-pip tiles late in the hand.
strategy.intermediate: Duplication is extreme, so plan for probabilistic availability rather than unique-tile tracking.
strategy.advanced: Shape the layout to keep your own exit options wide while narrowing opponent mobility at critical moments.
tips: Avoid narrow dependencies on a single value; with many players, the table state can swing quickly.
Prioritize flexible connectors and safe exits over speculative traps.

synthesis.shortDescription: Domijong is a four double-six set connecting game where heavy duplication shifts play toward mobility and robust end control.
